column3: A car windshield in the rain at night. Raindrops land and run on the glass with real droplet physics (drops merge, grow, and streak down), and the drops gather into the numerals, as if the time condenses out of the rain (design droplet numerals: beaded strokes of round, shaded water drops with a bright highlight each, no speckle; small drops merge into strokes). Street lights and traffic lights beyond blur into bokeh discs. Minute turn: the wiper blade sweeps a real arc round its pivot, the rubber blade flexing, a sheet of water pushed ahead of it, clearing the old digit, and the rain rebuilds the new one behind it. Hour: a car passes, its headlights flare through every drop, the wipers go double speed.

A rotary telephone dial in 3D perspective: the finger wheel with its holes, the chrome finger stop, a number card in the centre. The time is dialled: each minute an unseen finger dials the new minute, the wheel winds to the finger stop and whirrs back on its spring at the governor's steady speed, and the dialled digit appears on the centre card. Design numerals for the ring and the card in a mid-century telephone style. The hour lives on the card too, or on the dial's ring. Always alive: the phone rocks slightly, the coiled cord sways, a sheen slides over the chrome. Hour: the phone rings: the handset bounces in its cradle, the bells shake.

An armillary sphere in real 3D: nested brass rings (meridian, equator, ecliptic, an hour circle) around a small globe, turning slowly on their axes, with perspective, depth shading and correct occlusion where rings pass in front of each other. The hour is engraved on a big ring as numerals that rotate round to the front, the minutes on an inner ring, read against a fixed index pointer at the front. Design engraved numerals that foreshorten correctly on the curved rings and are big enough to read at 1x. Minute turn: the minute ring rotates to the new value with weight and overshoot. Hour: the whole sphere spins on its stand like a gyroscope and settles.

An arcade coin pusher in 3D perspective: two shelves of coins, the pusher plate sliding back and forth, coins dropping in from a chute, stacking, overlapping and tipping over the edge (round shaded coins in perspective, with rims and a highlight, never speckle). The time is the prize: chunky plastic numeral tokens sitting on the shelf among the coins, nudged a little with every push. Minute turn: a coin drop sets off a cascade, the old token teeters on the edge and falls into the win tray with a spray of coins, and a new token is dropped from the top and shoved into place. Hour: jackpot, a coin avalanche.

LEGO bricks in real 3D: each numeral is built from studded bricks (studs on top as small ellipses, shaded sides, seams between bricks), standing on a baseplate. Always alive: the camera orbits slowly, bricks wiggle as if a child's hand presses them. Minute turn: the old numeral's bricks are unclicked one by one and hop off onto a pile, then the new numeral is snapped together brick by brick from the pile, each dropping in with a click and a little squash. Hour: the whole model is dropped, explodes into pieces that bounce, and reassembles.

A bead maze toy (the kind in a doctor's waiting room): beads on bent wire tracks, in 3D perspective, the wires curving in and out of depth from a wooden base. The wires are bent into the numerals, and beads slide along them under gravity, bunching and clacking. Design the wire numerals as single continuous bent wires that read as digits, with the beads shaded as round spheres. Always alive: beads drift and slide, an unseen child's finger pushes a group up a wire now and then. Minute turn: the old digit's wire springs open with a wobble, its beads slide off onto the next wire, and the wire bends itself into the new numeral. Hour: every bead races around one big looping track.

Cardistry: a deck of playing cards in 3D, handled by unseen hands: riffle shuffles, a bridge (cards arched and cascading back), spring flourishes, fans, one-handed cuts, with real flex and perspective. The time is on the faces: the hour and minute cards are fanned out face up (design card faces with big bold indexes and pips in a crisp art-deco style). Always alive: the deck breathes, small cuts and flourishes, a card spins between fingers. Minute turn: the old minute cards are gathered into the deck, a riffle and a bridge, and the new minute cards are spun out face up. Hour: a spring flourish shoots the whole deck from hand to hand, then the new hour fans out.

A glass of soda in real 3D: ice cubes carved as the numerals float and bob, clink against each other and the glass, rotating slowly so their faces catch the light, bubbles rising (round, outlined, never speckle), a straw. Make ice read on a 1-bit panel: bold refracted edges, bright edge highlights, dark inner lines. Minute turn: the old ice numeral melts (shrinks, rounds, drips) and a new cube numeral is dropped in from above with a splash and a burst of fizz. Hour: the glass is refilled, foam overflowing.

Jack-in-the-box. Four little boxes with cranks; the numerals live on springs inside them: at rest each digit bobs on its coil spring above its open box, wobbling with squash and stretch, a clown-collar ruff under each. Design springy numerals that stretch and recoil but always read. Minute turn: the old digit is pushed down into its box, the lid snaps shut, the crank turns through the tune (tiny notes float up), the box trembles, and POP: the new digit springs out with a wild wobble that settles. Hour: all four pop together with confetti.

A chrome pop-up toaster in 3D, with two slices in the slots: the numerals are toasted into the bread (darker browning in the shape of the digits, shown when the toast is up). The heating coils glow through the slots while toasting, heat shimmer above, crumbs. Always alive: the lever trembles, the coils glow and dim, steam curls from the toast. Minute turn: POP: the toast with the old minute shoots up in an arc, flips and lands on a plate beside, and a fresh slice drops in, toasts, and rises with the new numeral browned into it. Hour: a big pop, both slices fly, a pat of butter lands on the hour.
